turns.content: For an ideal solute with concentration c(x), write the gravitational tidal force per mole in terms of the concentration profile.
Let a temperature profile decay exponentially as c0 exp(-x/lambda), and differentiate its logarithm.
If this exponential concentration profile falls by a factor of two over 10 cm, determine its spatial scale parameter in metres.
Combine the thermodynamic-force relation derived above with the exponential concentration gradient to obtain the x-component, including its sign.
Evaluate the force at 25 °C using T=298 K and R=8.3145 J mol^-1 K^-1, and state its direction relative to decreasing concentration.
Let +x point toward decreasing concentration. Under this convention, which way does the force act?
Show that this direction agrees with the sign of the x-component derived above.
Would changing the absolute scale c0 alter the magnitude, or does only the logarithmic gradient matter?
Report the molar force in N/mol and kN/mol, including its direction.
